titleEn: Starbase Tour with Everyday Astronaut — Part 2
titleZh: 与 Everyday Astronaut 一同参观星城基地——第2部分
summaryEn: Second part of the Starbase tour covering Starship hardware, heat shield tiles and stainless-steel structural choices.
summaryZh: 星城基地参观之旅的第2部分，涵盖星舰硬件、隔热瓦和不锈钢结构选型。

segments.textEn: Hi, it's me, Tim Dodd, the Everyday Astronaut. Welcome to part two of my tour of SpaceX's Starbase Factory with the ultimate tour guide, Elon Musk. If you haven't watched Part One, you obviously need to watch that because there's just gobs of information. And in this part, we're actually going to go inside the three main assembly tents, which is incredible!
segments.textZh: 嗨，是我，蒂姆·多德，Everyday Astronaut。欢迎观看我参观 SpaceX 星城基地工厂的第2部分，终极导游埃隆·马斯克将带我参观。如果你还没看过第1部分，那显然需要去看，因为里面有海量信息。而在这一部分，我们真的要进入3座主要装配帐篷，太不可思议了！

segments.textEn: And just like last time, we have a map that will occasionally pop up, courtesy of Ring Watchers on Twitter, that'll help you understand where exactly we are in the factory. We also have the YouTube play bar broken up into certain sections. We have links to those sections below, too. And we have an article up on our website that has some key points and takeaways of this conversation. The link and the description is below for that at www.
segments.textZh: 和上次一样，我们有一张地图会偶尔弹出，由 Twitter 上的 Ring Watchers 提供，它能帮助你了解我们在工厂里的确切位置。我们还把 YouTube 播放进度条划分成了若干部分。下方也有这些部分的链接。我们的网站上还有一篇文章，其中列出了这次对话的一些要点和收获。相关链接和说明就在下方，网址是 www。

segments.textEn: everydayastronaut. com. All right, let's go check out some Raptor engines. So, by the way, I think there's a good chance that ITAR and COMS might not want all this- - Oh, yeah, just... It just can't be any more than people are already getting from- - [Tim] That's true.
segments.textZh: everydayastronaut. com。好了，我们去看看一些猛禽发动机吧。所以，顺便说一句，我觉得 ITAR 和 COMS 很可能不希望看到所有这些——哦，是啊，只是……这些不能比人们已经从——[蒂姆] 那倒是。

segments.textEn: Telephoto lenses.
segments.textZh: 长焦镜头。

segments.textEn: [Tim] That, which is pretty much everything.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 那个，基本上就是一切了。

segments.textEn: And frankly, if some fool wants to copy this design, go for it. (Tim laughs) I mean, Raptor 2 is a giant improvement over this.
segments.textZh: 坦白说，如果哪个傻瓜想复制这个设计，那就尽管复制吧。（蒂姆笑）我的意思是，猛禽 2 相比这个有了巨大的改进。

segments.textEn: [Tim] What's the big simplifications you're hoping to have?
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 你希望实现哪些重大的简化？

segments.textEn: Well, maybe I shouldn't tell you all the secrets. (Tim laughs) We have funny things on the... We've got Pikachu over there.
segments.textZh: 嗯，也许我不该把所有秘密都告诉你。（蒂姆笑）我们在……上有些有趣的东西。那边有皮卡丘。

segments.textEn: [Tim] (laughs) I love that.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆]（笑）我喜欢那个。

segments.textEn: [Elon] Hello again.
segments.textZh: [埃隆] 又见面了。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Hello again. So that probably, I assume that means it's flown. Is that a flown one? (Elon laughs) - I don't know if this one's been flown.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 又见面了。所以我猜，那大概意味着它飞过了。这是一个飞过的吗？（埃隆笑）——我不知道这个是否飞过。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Geez. This really does look like that thing with all the NK33s. Those videos of- - Yeah, yeah, exactly. Engines that came back from the cold.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 天啊。这真的很像那个装满 NK33 的东西。那些关于——的视频——对，对，没错。从寒冷中归来的发动机。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Yes, seriously. It literally looks like that. This is insane. Man, that wrap vent is big. Geez.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 是的，说真的。它确实看起来就是那样。这太疯狂了。天啊，那个包裹式通风口真大。天啊。

segments.textEn: Yeah, I won't tell you all the secrets. (Tim laughs) You'll be able to see the difference very clearly.
segments.textZh: 是啊，我不会把所有秘密都告诉你。（蒂姆笑）你将能非常清楚地看到区别。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Okay.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 好的。

segments.textEn: And I guess, since the engines are... It's hard to have people not see them.
segments.textZh: 而且我想，既然发动机……很难不让人看到它们。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Yeah.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 对。

segments.textEn: They will... The Raptor 2 is visibly cleaner than Raptor 1. This sort of maze of plumbing and wiring doesn't exist on Raptor 2.
segments.textZh: 它们会……猛禽 2 明显比猛禽 1 简洁。猛禽 2 上没有这种迷宫般的管路和布线。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Although, it's already slimmed down a ton from like- - Yeah, it used to look like a frickin' Christmas tree.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 不过，它相比以前已经精简了很多——对，以前看起来就像一棵该死的圣诞树。

segments.textEn: [Tim] (laughs) Yeah.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆]（笑）对。

segments.textEn: You couldn't even see the engine for all the stuff that was around it.
segments.textZh: 周围全是东西，你甚至都看不到发动机。

segments.textEn: [Tim] No, you really couldn't. And now it's like, especially around the turbines and stuff, and the free burners, I mean, that used to be a whole, there's sensors every two millimeters.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 是啊，真的看不到。而现在，尤其是涡轮之类的周围，还有自由燃烧器，我是说，以前那完全就是，每隔 2 毫米就有一个传感器。

segments.textEn: [Elon] Yes.
segments.textZh: [埃隆] 是的。

segments.textEn: [Tim] So, Rap-Vac or Raptor-Vac has it's own regen channel on the extension, it looks like.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 所以，Rap-Vac 或 Raptor-Vac 的延伸段看起来有自己的再生冷却通道。

segments.textEn: [Elon] Yeah. That's a steel tube wall, raised steel tube wall.
segments.textZh: [埃隆] 对。那是钢管壁，凸起的钢管壁。

segments.textEn: [Tim] That looks great. And it has a different profile, too, that actually looks like the initial exit. Is there a different throat in it and everything? Or is it?
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 看起来很棒。而且它的轮廓也不同，实际上看起来像最初的出口。它的喉部和所有东西都不一样吗？还是说？

segments.textEn: [Elon] No. Throat's the same.
segments.textZh: [埃隆] 不。喉部是一样的。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Throat's the same?
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 喉部是一样的？

segments.textEn: It's just the part after the throat. The diverging section has different angles. Basically it's following a rail counter for a higher expansion ratio.
segments.textZh: 只是喉部之后的部分。扩张段的角度不同。基本上，它是按照导轨计数器来实现更高的膨胀比。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Yeah, yeah. What is the expansion ratio again? Is it like 150 or something?
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 对，对。膨胀比是多少来着？是大约 150 之类的吗？

segments.textEn: No. Man, I think we were... So this is actually, I think we were around 80-ish.
segments.textZh: 不是。天啊，我想我们当时……所以这个实际上，我想我们当时大约是 80 左右。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Oh, okay.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 哦，好的。

segments.textEn: But we wanna get to, we wanna do a little bit better. Maybe 90.
segments.textZh: 但我们想达到，我们想再做得好一点。也许是 90。

segments.textEn: [Tim] 'Cause you're already getting like, 380 ISP out of that thing, aren't you? Or I mean, sorry, yeah, 380.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 因为你们已经能从那东西上获得大约 380 的比冲了，不是吗？或者我是说，抱歉，对，380。

segments.textEn: 380's the aspirational number.
segments.textZh: 380 是期望达到的数字。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Okay.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 好的。

segments.textEn: But we should be able, I think we will get like 377 or 378.
segments.textZh: 但我们应该能够，我想我们会达到大约 377 或 378。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Okay, okay. And how are those coming along? It looks like obviously you've got a third one here. You've obviously made at least three.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 好的，好的。那些进展得怎么样？显然，看起来你们这里已经有第 3 台了。显然你们至少已经制造了 3 台。

segments.textEn: [Elon] Yeah.
segments.textZh: [埃隆] 对。

segments.textEn: [Tim] S-20's gonna have three.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] S-20 会有 3 台。

segments.textEn: [Elon] Yes.
segments.textZh: [埃隆] 是的。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Yes. Geez.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 是的。天哪。

segments.textEn: All the engines will have the same pumps and thrust-chamber assembly. It's really just building it one, sort of one variant that has a big nozzle and one variant that doesn't have thrust vector control actuators.
segments.textZh: 所有发动机都会采用相同的泵和推力室组件。实际上就是制造它，一种算是带有大型喷管的型号，以及一种没有推力矢量控制执行器的型号。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Okay, okay. And that's gonna be the difference between the R boost and the?
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 好的，好的。这就是 R boost 和那个之间的区别？

segments.textEn: Yeah. I mean, it's basically the same engine, minus PVC.
segments.textZh: 对。我的意思是，它基本上是同一台发动机，只是少了 PVC。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Gotcha. So, the outer shells that you're working on for the GSE are 12 meters.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 明白了。所以，你们正在为 GSE 制作的外壳是 12 米。

segments.textEn: There's a Raptor without the stuff; looks practically naked.
segments.textZh: 那里有一台去掉那些东西的猛禽发动机；看起来简直是赤裸的。

segments.textEn: [Tim] (laughs) you're like, actually that's secretly version two. It's super simple. No.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆]（笑）你会说，其实那暗地里就是第 2 版。它超级简单。不。

segments.textEn: [Elon] Version two will look a bit like that actually.
segments.textZh: [埃隆] 第 2 版实际上会看起来有点像那样。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Really?
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 真的吗？

segments.textEn: [Elon] It's very tight.
segments.textZh: [埃隆] 非常紧凑。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Really?
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 真的吗？

segments.textEn: [Elon] Yeah.
segments.textZh: [埃隆] 对。

segments.textEn: [Tim] I mean, again, when you look at some of those Soviet engines, they were also incredibly simple looking. I'm guessing they just obviously didn't have 'em wired to the gills with electronics, though, either. You know?
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 我是说，还是那句话，当你看那些苏联发动机时，它们看起来也简单得不可思议。不过我猜，显然它们也没有浑身上下都布满电子设备的线路。你明白吧？

segments.textEn: They didn't. They simply didn't, back in those days, they did not have good electronics.
segments.textZh: 它们没有。它们确实没有，在那个年代，它们没有好的电子设备。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Right.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 对。

segments.textEn: So there's nothing to- - [Tim] There's nothing to wire up.
segments.textZh: 所以没什么可——[蒂姆] 没什么需要接线的。

segments.textEn: Yeah.
segments.textZh: 对。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Yeah. How much, I feel like you iterate this quite a bit and remind people that it's, failure kind of is an option. Why do you think people are so afraid to fail? And why do you embrace it? How do you teach that culture even, that it's okay? When you're not even trying to like... You know, SN-8 is a perfect example. You weren't trying to do a mission. You're just trying to get data out of the thing.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 对。多大程度上，我感觉你经常反复强调这一点，并提醒人们，失败在某种意义上是一个选项。你觉得人们为什么如此害怕失败？而你为什么会接受失败？你又是怎样教导这种文化的，让人们知道失败没关系？当你甚至并不是想要……你知道，SN-8就是一个绝佳的例子。你们并不是要执行一项任务。你们只是想从这东西上获得数据。

segments.textEn: Yeah. We have just a fundamentally different optimization for Starship versus say, like the polar extreme would be Dragon. Dragon, there can be no failures ever. Everything's gotta be tested six ways to Sunday. There has to be tons of margin. There can never be a failure ever for any reason whatsoever.
segments.textZh: 对。我们对星舰采用的优化方式从根本上就不同于，比如说，处在另一个极端的龙飞船。龙飞船绝对不能发生任何故障。所有东西都必须以各种方式彻底测试。必须留有大量裕度。绝对不能出于任何原因发生任何故障。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Yeah.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 对。

segments.textEn: That's extreme conservatism. Then Falcon is a little less conservative. It is possible for us to have, say, a failure of the booster on landing. That's not the end of the world.
segments.textZh: 那是极端保守主义。然后猎鹰要稍微没那么保守。比如说，我们的助推器在着陆时可能会发生故障。那并不是世界末日。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Right.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 对。

segments.textEn: And then for Starship, it's like the polar opposite of Dragon: we're iterating rapidly in order to create the first ever fully reusable rocket, orbital rocket. And fully and rapidly reusable. Reusable in a way that is like an aircraft. Rapidly reusable rockets.
segments.textZh: 而对于星舰，它就像是龙飞船的另一个极端：我们正在快速迭代，以制造有史以来第一枚完全可重复使用的火箭，轨道火箭。而且是能够完全且快速重复使用。以像飞机一样的方式重复使用。可快速重复使用的火箭。

segments.textEn: [Tim] It's a big deal.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 这意义重大。

segments.textEn: Yeah. That's the fundamental Holy Grail for making life multi-planetary.
segments.textZh: 对。那是实现生命多行星化的根本圣杯。

segments.textEn: [Tim] where do you think the Space Shuttle failed in being, and definitely rapidly would be a word you've got to scratch off the list- - Yeah, definitely not rapid.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 你认为航天飞机在哪些方面没能做到，而“快速”肯定是一个你必须从清单上划掉的词——对，肯定不快。

segments.textEn: [Tim] But where do you think it failed? And where do you think... What lessons have you learned that you know you're not going to be making on Starship?
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 但你觉得它失败在哪里？还有你认为……你吸取了哪些教训，让你知道自己不会在星舰上犯同样的错误？

segments.textEn: The Space Shuttle had almost no room for iteration because there were people on board. So you couldn't be blowing up shuttles. So that's a big problem.
segments.textZh: 航天飞机几乎没有迭代空间，因为上面载着人。所以你不能让航天飞机爆炸。因此这是一个大问题。

segments.textEn: [Tim] They did very, very little.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 他们做得非常、非常少。

segments.textEn: Very little. In fact, a lack of iteration was the problem. Because a lot of the issues they were aware of, but people were too afraid to make change.
segments.textZh: 非常少。事实上，缺乏迭代就是问题所在。因为很多问题他们都知道，但人们太害怕做出改变。

segments.textEn: [Tim] 'Cause the design froze.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 因为设计被冻结了。

segments.textEn: Yeah, 'cause it's like... Yeah. I mean, there was a risk/reward asymmetry. So, big punishment for, if you make a change and something goes wrong, big punishment. If you make a change and it goes right, small reward.
segments.textZh: 是啊，因为这就像……是啊。我的意思是，风险与回报是不对称的。所以，如果你做出改变而出了问题，惩罚很大，惩罚很大。如果你做出改变而结果正确，回报很小。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Yup, yup.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 对，对。

segments.textEn: So, the issues with the O-ring and then with the insulation coming off and hitting the wing, they had seen this before.
segments.textZh: 所以，O形密封圈的问题，以及隔热材料脱落并撞击机翼的问题，他们以前都见过。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Yeah, they were known.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 是的，这些问题是已知的。

segments.textEn: They were known issues. Because it had worked before, they're like, well, it worked before. Russian roulette works before.
segments.textZh: 这些都是已知问题。因为以前成功过，他们就会说，好吧，以前成功过。俄罗斯轮盘赌以前也成功过。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Right. (chuckles) Oh God.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 对。（轻笑）天啊。

segments.textEn: [Elon] Look, I've pulled the trigger so many times. There must be no bullets in this gun.
segments.textZh: [埃隆] 你看，我已经扣动扳机这么多次了。这把枪里肯定没有子弹。

segments.textEn: [Tim] It must be no problem.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 肯定没问题。

segments.textEn: [Elon] Yeah. Anyway, it's hard to iterate, though, when people are on every mission. You can't just be blowing stuff up 'cause you're gonna kill people. Starship does not have anyone on board so we can blow things up. That's really helpful.
segments.textZh: [埃隆] 是啊。不管怎样，不过每次任务都载人时，很难进行迭代。你不能就这么把东西炸掉，因为那会害死人。星舰上没有任何人，所以我们可以把东西炸掉。这真的很有帮助。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Do you have any considerations yet on any kind of launch escape? Are you just hoping that by the time you put people on it, you've flown it say 100, 200 times, and you're familiar with all the failure modes, and you've mitigated it to a high degree of confidence. Or what's your?
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 你们是否已经考虑过任何类型的发射逃逸系统？还是说，你只是希望等到让人乘坐它时，它已经飞过，比如说100、200次，你们熟悉了所有故障模式，并且已经将其缓解到高度可信的程度。或者你的想法是？

segments.textEn: Yeah. Larger scale, I think is... Yeah, you basically just need to fly a lot and have a lot of redundancy. So if you lose an engine on the booster, it doesn't matter basically. If you lose multiple engines it shouldn't matter. And you should be able to lose an engine on the ship and everything's okay. Launch escape is basically just protecting you for the ascent phase. And actually most launch escape systems only protect you for a small part of the ascent phase. 'Cause the typical launch escape system is a solid rocket motor on the tip of the capsule, which then has to be...
segments.textZh: 是的。更大尺度上，我认为是……是的，基本上你只需要进行大量飞行，并且拥有大量冗余。所以，如果助推器损失1台发动机，基本上没关系。如果损失多台发动机，也应该没关系。而且飞船损失1台发动机后，一切也应该没问题。发射逃逸系统基本上只能在上升阶段保护你。而实际上，大多数发射逃逸系统只能在上升阶段的一小部分时间里保护你。因为典型的发射逃逸系统是位于飞船舱顶端的一台固体火箭发动机，之后必须被……

segments.textEn: [Tim] It has to be jettisoned.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 必须被抛弃。

segments.textEn: It has to be jettisoned on every mission. So, if it's not jettisoned, the crew dies.
segments.textZh: 每次任务中都必须将它抛弃。所以，如果没有把它抛弃，机组人员就会死亡。

segments.textEn: [Tim] That's a failure mode, right there.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 这本身就是一种故障模式。

segments.textEn: That's a failure mode. So you have a state change post liftoff, which is bad. Then because the damn thing's so heavy, they also can't carry it all the way to orbit. So, they'll typically jettison the escape system shortly after second stage ignition or final stage ignition. So that you don't have escape all the way to orbit even. Now, at least with Dragon, we have escape all the way to orbit. So that's, I think, a safety improvement. There's no escape system coming back to Earth. That's doesn't exist.
segments.textZh: 这是一种故障模式。所以升空之后会发生一次状态改变，这是不好的。然后，因为那该死的东西太重了，他们也无法一路把它带入轨道。所以，他们通常会在第二级点火或末级点火后不久抛弃逃逸系统。因此，你甚至无法一路拥有逃逸能力直到进入轨道。现在，至少在龙飞船上，我们一路到轨道都拥有逃逸能力。所以我认为这是一项安全改进。返回地球时没有逃逸系统。那种东西不存在。

segments.textEn: [Tim] Right.
segments.textZh: [蒂姆] 对。

segments.textZh: 但对于俯仰，你基本上得把助推器压下去。所以，你得把这个庞然大物压进气流里，而它并不想往那里去。你需要的俯仰力，也就是这里需要的力最大。所以，让两对翼面靠得更近，更像X翼战斗机，能让它们对俯仰发挥更大的作用。
